business.what_it_does: Non-bank lender to retail and small-business borrowers, in three areas: vehicle finance; secured SME lending (LAP, SME and SBPL); and consumer lending, which covers home loans, CSEL (unsecured business, personal and professional loans, consumer durables and digital lending) and a new gold-loan book. AUM was INR2,68,009 crore at Q2 FY27, up 25% YoY.

segments.name: Vehicle Finance
segments.comment: Revenue share not stated. 48% of AUM (INR1,29,787 crore, +21% YoY) and ~50% of Q2 FY27 disbursements (INR17,801 crore, +31%) (C1).

segments.name: Secured SME (LAP, SME, SBPL)
segments.comment: Q2 FY27 disbursements INR9,345 crore, +42% YoY, ~26% of the total (C1). AUM not stated.

segments.name: Home Loans
segments.comment: FY26 AUM +23% YoY (C4). Guided at 25%+ growth with LAP for FY27 (G22).

segments.name: CSEL
segments.comment: ~3.6% pre-tax ROA, with >4% targeted (C3). AUM grew only 4% in FY26 after exiting partnership-led businesses (C4).

segments.name: Gold Loans
segments.comment: New: INR1,130 crore disbursed in Q4 FY26 (C4). AUM of INR2,000 crore-plus, with INR5,000 crore targeted for FY27 (G13).

credibility.label: medium
credibility.summary: Chola raised its FY27 growth guide twice (20-23% to 22-23% to ~25%) and trimmed credit-cost guidance from 1.5% to 1.4%, and Q2 AUM +25% and PAT +40.5% back that up. Against that, the cost-of-funds outlook doubled from ~10bps to ~20bps within a quarter, and no closed-period target can be checked against reported numbers.

promises.evidence: Q2 FY27 AUM grew 25% YoY to INR2,68,009 crore on 47% disbursement growth (C1), in line with the target. The ledger calls this guidance 'held', but it is above the 20-23% (G17) and 22-23% (G11) given on the two prior calls, so in practice it was raised.

H1 FY27 credit cost is not in the inputs. The guide improved from ~1.5% (G16) to ~1.4%. A Q2 margin of 23.6% against 20.9% a year earlier and PAT up 40.5% fit lower credit costs but don't prove the number.
No opex ratio is reported in the inputs. The range's upper end is 10bps above the ~3% FY27 guide (G20).
Superseded by the ~25% guide on the Q2 FY27 call (G1). Q2 AUM growth of 25% (C1) is running above this 22-23% range.
Gold-loan AUM after Q1 FY27 is not in the inputs. The target needs about 2.5x growth from INR2,000 crore-plus within the year.
Raised twice since (22-23% in G11, ~25% in G1). Q2 FY27 AUM growth of 25% (C1) is above the 23% top end.

FY26 closing AUM growth is not in the inputs. The Q4 FY26 call said election-related documentation delays hit LAP and home-loan disbursements but not overall asset growth (C5). Revenue grew 19.5% YoY in Q4 FY26 (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct).
A 2-3 year target. The near-term opex ratio is guided at 3.0-3.1% (G4), so it needs a 20-30bps reduction.
No window was given and no cost-of-funds figure is in the inputs. The ~20bps is double the ~10bps H2 FY27 rise guided one quarter earlier (G15).
October 2026 has ended, but no disbursement figure for it is in the inputs. The guide implies a sharp slowdown from 47% disbursement growth in Q2 FY27 (C1).

Medium-term target. The two CSEL businesses are at ~3.6% pre-tax ROA (C3), and consumer PBT ROTA has been above 3-3.5% for about three quarters (C2). Segment financials are not disclosed, so progress can't be tracked from reported numbers.
Board approval only; shareholder and regulatory approvals are outstanding. For context, D/E is 6.72 (F:debt_to_equity), and Tier 1 capital was 14.12% at December 2025 (C7).

The quote ('we have been talking about 3.5%') matches the CSEL target in G28 rather than company-level guidance, which was only above 3% (G18). CSEL is at ~3.6% pre-tax ROA (C3). Company-level pre-tax ROA is not in the inputs.

One quarter later, the Q2 FY27 call guided cost of funds up ~20bps (G6) against ~10bps here. G6 gives no window, so this assumes the same H2 period. The drift list misses it because the two items carry different metric labels.
The guide was improved to ~1.4% on the Q2 FY27 call (G2), as the drift list shows. This rests on management's revised guide; the H1 actual credit cost is not in the inputs.

ROA was already 3.2% in Q3 FY26 (C7), and Q2 FY27 PAT growth of 40.5% (F:pat_yoy_last_q_pct) outpaced AUM growth of 25% (C1), so returns on assets are rising. The inputs give no FY27 company pre-tax ROA.
No NIM figure is in the inputs. The cost of funds is now guided up ~20bps (G6), a headwind to holding 8%.
In Q2 FY27, vehicle-finance AUM grew 21% YoY to INR1,29,787 crore and disbursements 31% (C1), both above the guided ~18% and 15-20%.
No H1 FY27 home-loan or LAP AUM growth is in the inputs. Home-loan AUM grew 23% in FY26 (C4), below this bar. Secured-SME disbursements, which include LAP, grew 42% in Q2 FY27 (C1).
No CSEL credit-loss figure is in the inputs. The Q2 FY27 call still names lower net credit costs as the main lever for CSEL profitability (C3).
The CSEL businesses are at ~3.6% pre-tax ROA (C3), above 3.5%. The target didn't say whether it was pre- or post-tax.
Product-mix shares are not in the inputs. Gold-loan AUM of INR2,000 crore-plus (G13) is under 1% of INR2,68,009 crore AUM (C1), but CSEL size is not given.
The Q2 FY27 call reiterated a 3.0-3.1% near-term range (G4), at or up to 10bps above this guide. The actual ratio is not in the inputs.
No ROTA figure is in the inputs, and the scope is unclear: company-level pre-tax ROA was guided only above 3% (G18), so 4.2% probably refers to one segment.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Growth is broad-based across vehicle finance, SME and consumer, and running ahead of plan (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: AUM grew 25% YoY and vehicle-finance AUM 21%. Revenue growth accelerated every quarter, from 17.3% to 23.8%, and PAT rose 40.5%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Credit costs are falling, from a 1.5% guide to ~1.4% (G16, G2, C6).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Margin at 23.6% against 20.9% a year earlier, and PAT growing 16.7 points faster than revenue, fit that story. But the margin is still 570bps below three years ago, and the H1 credit-cost figure itself is not in the inputs.
Q2 disbursements grew 47%, but October was guided at only ~18% (G7). Whether 25% AUM growth holds if H2 disbursement growth runs near that pace can't be tested from the inputs yet.

bull.point: The growth guide was raised twice and is being met: FY27 guidance went from 20-23% to 22-23% to ~25%, and Q2 FY27 AUM grew 25% to INR2,68,009 crore on 47% disbursement growth.
Profit is outgrowing the book: PAT rose 40.5% YoY against revenue growth of 23.8%, the margin was 23.6% against 20.9% a year earlier, and the credit-cost guide was cut from 1.5% to 1.4%.
ROE is 19.0%, and CSEL's ~3.6% pre-tax ROA already beats its 3.5% FY27 target, with more than 4% guided for the medium term.

bear.point: Funding costs are rising faster than guided: the expected cost-of-funds increase went from ~10bps in H2 (Q1 FY27 call) to ~20bps (Q2 FY27 call), while NIM is guided flat at ~8%.
Growth is consuming capital: D/E is 6.72 on INR2,31,911 crore of borrowings, and the board has approved raising up to INR5,000 crore.
Momentum may fade: October disbursements were guided at ~18% against 47% in Q2. The 3-year PAT CAGR of 25.2% trails the revenue CAGR of 34.2%, and the margin is 570bps below three years ago.

questions: October disbursement growth was guided at ~18% against 47% in Q2. What was the actual figure, which products slowed, and what H2 disbursement growth does the ~25% AUM target assume?
The expected H2 cost-of-funds rise doubled from ~10bps to ~20bps in one quarter. What drove it, and what FY27 NIM does it leave against the ~8% guide?
What were H1 FY27 net credit cost and CSEL credit loss against the 1.4% and sub-5% targets, and at what Tier 1 level would you draw on the INR5,000 crore raise?
